title: POC Deployment Criteria - Horizon Telemetry
summary: Initial POC scoping to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment for telemetry NLP workloads. Covered success criteria (latency, throughput, cost, quality/regression), workload sizing (concurrency, avg seq len, tokens/day), benchmark plan, and a 6-week POC timeline. Security and data residency constraints flagged as key decision drivers.
topics: deployment tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated vs private
next_steps: Redwood to share Dedicated vs Private delta sheet and sample pricing (Maya) - due 2026-01-20
Horizon to provide 2 weeks of production traces and a representative prompt set (Priya) - due 2026-01-22
Schedule in-region latency baseline run (AE + SE + Horizon infra) - week of 2026-01-26
action_items: Maya Patel | Share pricing delta and Dedicated sizing template | Due 2026-01-20
Liam O'Connor | Draft benchmark harness (load profile + eval scripts) and run a smoke test on hosted sandbox | Due 2026-01-23
Priya Singh | Export 14 days of request logs, 95th/99th percentile seq lengths, and sample prompts | Due 2026-01-22
Alex Rivera | Confirm compliance contacts and KMS/HSM requirements | Due 2026-01-24
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-17 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Alex (Horizon CTO), Priya (ML Infra), Jon (Product)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda — confirm success criteria for the PoC, go over rough workload numbers, decide which deployment modes we should validate first, and agree timeline.
[00:18] Alex: yep, thanks. we want to understand if hosted is feasible for us or if we need Dedicated or full Private — we have telemetry data that is somewhat sensitive, and some customers need data residency in eu-west-1.
[00:34] Priya: and just to add, we have compliance hoops — SOC 2 in the roadmap and we use a corporate KMS, we can't have keys outside our control for certain classes of logs.
[00:45] Liam: got it. at a high level we'll look at three knobs: latency targets (p95/p99), throughput (req/s and tokens/s), and cost per 1M tokens — plus quality regressions.
[00:58] Jon: on quality, we won't accept more than a 2% regression on intent classification accuracy on our internal eval set, otherwise we need fallback to a higher-accuracy model.
[01:12] Maya: that's a good hard gate. can you give ballpark traffic? concurrency, avg seq length?
[01:20] Priya: baseline is small — ~50 rps average, 250 rps peak during ingest bursts. avg seq length is ~220 tokens, 95th is ~860 tokens, we do longer historical queries sometimes. tokens/day around 120M but highly spiky.
[01:41] Liam: okay that's helpful. that pattern favors batching and cache for repeated prefixes — we can propose prefix K V cache and controlled batching on Dedicated. hosted can handle it too but cost may be higher on sustained duty.
[01:58] Alex: when you say K V cache do you mean KV, like key-value cache? sometimes transcripts change that to 'K V' and it's confusing.
[02:06] Liam: yeah, KV cache — sorry, transcription habit. the idea is to reuse cached past kv states for repeated contexts to cut tokens.
[02:14] Priya: any concerns with multitenant hosted from a data isolation standpoint? some of our enterprise customers require no egress of raw logs.
[02:23] Maya: hosted can be configured with strong data retention controls and redaction hooks, but for strict no-egress we'd usually recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed networking or VPC peering.
[02:36] Jon: what's the friction to get Dedicated up — is it weeks or months?
[02:41] Liam: typically Dedicated provisioning is a few weeks for sandbox + load testing, production Dedicated pools for SLA usually 4–6 weeks depending on capacity and contract, whereas Private (VPC or on-prem) takes longer, often 6–12 weeks, because of network and KMS setup and air-gap if needed.
[02:57] Alex: what about latency numbers? our SLO is 150 ms p95 for short routing queries, but longer analytics calls can be 500–800 ms and that's ok.
[03:09] Liam: short inferences with the right model and quantization profile on Dedicated we can hit sub-100 ms p95 for 64-token responses; for 200–800 token responses it's more about throughput and batching — you should expect p95 to scale up. hosted numbers are similar but we recommend Dedicated for strict p95 SLAs.
[03:27] Priya: quantization — we use some 4-bit quantized models internally for cost reasons; does Redwood support quantized variants and how does that affect accuracy?
[03:37] Liam: yes, runtime supports quantization-friendly paths. we'll surface model-specific expected quality deltas — that's part of the benchmark plan. often you see small accuracy shifts; we'll include those thresholds in the eval.
[03:50] Jon: ok, so success criteria summary — say: p95 < 150 ms for quick routes, throughput 250 rps peak sustained, cost target <= $X per 1M tokens (we'll provide internal target), and <2% quality regression.
[04:05] Maya: I noted that. we're going to need sample prompts and traces to size Dedicated properly. Priya, can you export a 2-week sample?
[04:12] Priya: yes we can do 14 days with anonymized request IDs, seq lengths and payload sizes. we'll need guidance on anonymization.
[04:20] Maya: we'll send a template for anonymization — remove PII, keep tokenized lengths and the prompt buckets.
[04:26] Alex: benchmarks — what's the harness look like? load profile, synthetic vs replay?
[04:31] Liam: we recommend three phases: 1) replay of production traces in a sandbox hosted environment to see functional correctness and baseline latencies; 2) synthetic stress tests to hit peak tokens/s for throughput and batching behaviors; 3) model quality evals against your labeled eval set for regression.
[04:52] Maya: timeline suggestion: week0 (this week) — exchange artifacts and pricing; week1 — hosted baseline replay on our sandbox and initial metrics; week2-3 — Dedicated sizing run and quantization tests; week4 — integration and UAT; week6 — final performance validation and go/no-go. that's roughly 6 weeks.
[05:11] Alex: that aligns with our Q1 goals. we prefer to test hosted first to get quick wins and then pivot to Dedicated if cost or latency doesn't meet gates.
[05:20] Jon: any concerns about model fallbacks, like doing canary and automatic fallback to a smaller model when load spikes?
[05:27] Liam: yes, Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallbacks to cheaper model variants or region-based fallbacks. we'll show routing policy configs in the console.
[05:38] Priya: security — we need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration. do you support customer-managed keys in Private?
[05:47] Maya: yes for Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM. Dedicated has options for KMS integration and VPC peering; hosted supports encrypted-at-rest and can offer KMS integration for dedicated customers. we'll add a security appendix.
[06:00] Alex: any red flags we should know about with long sequences (800+ tokens)?
[06:06] Liam: memory/kv management becomes critical, and latency distribution widens. we'll probably recommend request-level batching thresholds and middle-tier prefix caching for analytics queries. also consider truncation policies for extremely long histories.
[06:21] Priya: do you have metrics for sustained cost per token with batching? we want to understand marginal token cost when reuse is high.
[06:29] Liam: yes, our Optimize toolkit can simulate cost with different cache hit rates and batch sizes. we'll run a simulation for your trace.
[06:37] Jon: competitor question — we looked at Anthropic and some self-host options. what are the typical reasons customers pick Redwood over those?
[06:45] Maya: usually it's the combined production runtime (latency + batching), transparent cost controls, and operations tooling — e.g., tracing hooks, rollouts, and fallback policies. for on-prem needs Redwood Private can match self-host while removing the orchestration burden.
[06:59] Alex: good. about benchmarks — can you run a P95 and P99 breakdown by token length buckets (0-128, 129-512, 513-1024)?
[07:09] Liam: yes we'll include bucketed latency histograms and tail latencies. also tokenization variance will be included.
[07:17] Maya: for gating — if hosted sandbox fails p95 by more than 30% we escalate to Dedicated sizing run; if Dedicated fails gating we'll consider Private but that adds lead time.
[07:28] Priya: what's the procurement implication for Dedicated — any minimum commitment?
[07:33] Maya: Dedicated typically needs a reserved capacity contract for production SLAs; we can do a pilot with short-term reserved credits. we'll include options in the pricing doc.
[07:42] Jon: and how will we validate quality regression automatically? we want automated regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
[07:50] Liam: Redwood Optimize supports continuous quality monitoring and can trigger alerts when a metric drops below a threshold. we'll wire that into your eval suite.
[07:59] Alex: ok, I'd like to recap next steps. Maya, you'll send pricing and Dedicated vs Private delta. Liam, you'll draft the benchmark harness and run a hosted sandbox replay. Priya will export traces.
[08:15] Maya: yes. I'll also include a security appendix for KMS and SAML options and a short decision matrix template.
[08:23] Priya: timeline note — we have a security review cycle that might add 1–2 weeks for Private if we go that route.
[08:30] Maya: noted; we'll mark that as a risk.
[08:35] Jon: any other blockers?
[08:37] Alex: none from me. let's schedule the baseline replay for next Tuesday.
[08:42] Maya: great. thanks everyone.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts and misrecognized product names (e.g., 'K V cache'), some filler words left in. Speaker attributions were confirmed by host at end.

End of meeting.
